newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-Dec 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-Dec 24.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- MING PAO -- During the first meeting between the Governor Chris Patten and Hong Kong's leader-designate Tung Chee-hwa, they failed to change each other's view on the provisional legislature but decided to meet more often.

-- A Beijing official said Chinese leader Deng Xiaoping might not be able to come to Hong Kong for the 1997 handover ceremony. Starting from New Year's Day, Beijing's Central Television would broadcast a documentary on Deng for five days.

-- WEN WEI PO -- Director of the New China News Agency Zhou Nan said the political atmosphere in Hong Kong had changed significantly of late, and there were no insurpassable barriers blocking the way to the handover.
-- A major exhibition on Hong Kong past, present and future, held jointly by the Hong Kong and Macau Affairs Office and the New China News Agency, will be staged in March in Beijing.

-- SING TAO -- It was generally believed there were 900 million peasants in China but recent research showed the number had fallen to 250 million because many peasants had moved to towns and cities and taken on other jobs. The trend would continue in the next few years.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Real estate developers voiced strong oppositinn to any further government controls on property sales which they said would increase transaction costs and hurt liquidity in the market.
-- Mitsubishi Motors' plan to set up a car joint venture in Hunan province with the long-term aim of a stock market flotation was approved by the State Planning Commission.
-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- The cost of living accelerated in November as retailers put up prices in response to a steady increase in customer demand.
